Animation sources

Our backgrounds combine published imaging, measured anatomy, and illustrative animation. No source implies endorsement of Valus.

Cardiac MRI

Real-time MRI of a human heart (2-chamber view), Shuo Zhang, Martin Uecker, Dirk Voit, Klaus-Dietmar Merboldt, and Jens Frahm, 2010. Original publication. Licensed CC BY 2.0.

The original 463 × 463 footage is transcoded to WebM, looped, scaled, and feathered into the page background. We do not invent scan detail or interpolate anatomy. Original footage · Web version.

Neuron reconstruction

cnic_001 / NMO_1, Wearne/Hof archive, retrieved through NeuroMorpho.Org (RRID:SCR_002145). CC BY 4.0 reuse terms. Source 3D reconstruction.

This is a rhesus macaque prefrontal layer-3 pyramidal neuron reconstruction containing soma and dendrites, not an axon or a human brain network. The visualization repeats and transforms the measured skeleton, thickens fine structures for visibility, and adds illustrative spines, organelles, surface shading, and traveling fluorescent signals. The colors and activity are not recorded electrophysiology.

  • Original reconstruction publications: doi:10.1016/S0306-4522(02)00305-6 and doi:10.1093/cercor/13.9.950.
  • Tecuatl C, Ljungquist B, Ascoli GA (2024). Accelerating the continuous community sharing of digital neuromorphology data. FASEB Bioadv. 6(7):207–221. doi:10.1096/fba.2024-00048.
  • Adapted geometry and visualization additions based on this reconstruction are available under CC BY 4.0, attribution: Valus and the reconstruction sources above.

Visual research

Dendritic Spines in a Hippocampal Neuron, Miquel Bosch, Bear Lab, Picower Institute, MIT, provided a microscopy reference for spine shapes. The reference photograph is not redistributed in this website.

We also evaluated Versal’s neuron mesh, Ehab Shalout’s animated heart cross-section, and Allen Cell Types. These assets are not included.
